junction.name: Utica Avenue & Church Avenue, New York City

claims.text: Utica Avenue & Church Avenue had 40 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 14 pedestrians injured, 1 cyclist injured and 0 people killed.
These counts are Utica Avenue & Church Avenue's own: the city's record places 43 of the 144 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $2.7 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's priority junctions.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.2 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $411,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 0.6 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $214,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Utica Avenue, Church Avenue (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 45, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 17.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 45, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 17
Subject: Request for safety review at Utica Avenue & Church Avenue

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We are writing to ask you to carry out a safety study at the junction of Utica Avenue & Church Avenue, for the roads you are responsible for, and to consider fixes on those roads.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 69 crashes, of which 40 were injury crashes. 14 pedestrians and 1 cyclist were injured. The city lists this junction as a priority location. No one was killed in this period according to the records checked. The yearly cost of the harm, in the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), was 2.7 million dollars per year. No safety work is recorded in this period; the latest recorded project was a Leading Pedestrian Interval signal in 2005.

We ask you to consider two low-cost fixes on your roads, subject to a site check:

- Reflective backplates on the traffic signals, which is expected to prevent about 1.2 injury crashes per year. This needs a site check for an entry on yellow or red.
- Longer yellow signal times, which is expected to prevent about 0.6 injury crashes per year. This needs a site check for an entry on yellow or red, and whether the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.

Please let us know the outcome of the study and next steps.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

- NYC Open Data, Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes (h9gi-nx95)
- NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (corridors); NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (intersections); NYC Vision Zero View, Enhanced Crossings (6ax4-q5k4); NYC Vision Zero View, Leading Pedestrian Interval Signals; NYC Vision Zero View, Signal Timing/25 MPH Retiming; NYC Vision Zero View, Speed Humps (jknp-skuy); NYC Vision Zero View, Turn Traffic Calming; NYC Vision Zero priority corridors; NYC Vision Zero priority intersections
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 1410 (reflective backplates on the traffic signals)
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 4219 (longer yellow signal times)
- U.S. DOT Benefit-Cost Analysis Guidance, 2026 Update, Table A-1 (2024 dollars)
